entries.title: Top-ranked Mount Carmel reloads for a five-peat with 19 future college football players
entries.summary: <p>Mount Carmel opened last season as “<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2025/08/25/mount-carmel-high-school-football-chicago-preview" >the most talented team in Chicago history</a>” with eight major college recruits. The state’s most successful and controversial team is even better this year.</p><p>The Caravan has five Power Four committed players, another eight players with Power Four offers and 19 total future college football players. Expect more to be added as the season moves along.</p><p>That doesn’t even count the talented high school football players the program is producing. Jordan Lynch’s squad, No. 1 in the preseason Super 25, has reloaded as it attempts to win a fifth consecutive state championship and record 18th overall state championship.</p><p>“Last year was the first time in Mount Carmel history that we went undefeated as a program,” Lynch said. “36-0. Our lower levels are good, and now we get that class in. This is more depth than we’ve had in the past.”</p><p>Both lines are loaded with large, talented future college players. Senior Quentin Burrell (Michigan) and junior Marshaun Thornton may be the best wide receiver duo in state history.</p><p>Linebacker Roman Igwebuike (Notre Dame) and defensive back Tavares Harrington (Michigan) are the most battle-tested defensive stars in the area.</p><p>“There should be no doubt about going 14-0 and winning [state],” Burrell said. “It would be the worst year we could have if we don’t do it.”</p><p>The Caravan features a new starting quarterback again, which appears to be the only possible chink in the team’s armor. Senior Ryder Startz, the backup last year, beat out Plainfield East transfer Brady Cloherty for the starting job. Talented sophomore Thomas Elliott is also waiting in the wings.</p><p>“There was a healthy quarterback competition in July,” Lynch said. “Brady has done a great job and had a great attitude. He is still learning and adjusting to Mount Carmel, to a new offense and what Catholic League football is about. He has kept a great mindset, competing and working every day. You never know. He is one play away.”</p><p>Lynch is impressed with Startz’s decision-making and speed.</p><p>“He does a good job, and we have tons of playmakers around him to help him, so when he is going through his growing pains, they can get him out of trouble,” Lynch said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-790000" name="html-embed-module-790000"></a><blockquote class="tiktok-embed" cite="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports/video/7675425781530512671" data-video-id="7675425781530512671" style="max-width: 605px;min-width: 325px;" > <section> <a target="_blank" title="@michaelsobriensports" href="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports?refer=embed">@michaelsobriensports</a> Mount Carmel opens the season as No. 1 in the preseason Super 25. Michigan recruit Quentin Burrell is confident the Caravan will pull off a state title five-peat. <a title="ihsa" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/ihsa?refer=embed">#ihsa</a> <a title="football" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/football?refer=embed">#football</a> <a title="mountcarmel" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/mountcarmel?refer=embed">#mountcarmel</a> <a title="chicago" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/chicago?refer=embed">#chicago</a> <a title="michigan" target="_blank" href="https://www.tiktok.com/tag/michigan?refer=embed">#michigan</a> <a target="_blank" title="♬ original sound - michaelsobriensports" href="https://www.tiktok.com/music/original-sound-7675425728992742175?refer=embed">♬ original sound - michaelsobriensports</a> </section> </blockquote> <script async src="https://www.tiktok.com/embed.js"></script> </div> </div><p>There won’t be much time for growing pains. The Caravan opens at ISU against highly regarded East St. Louis, another team loaded with major college talent, and then faces New Jersey power St. Joseph on ESPN in Week 2.</p><p>Mount Carmel has become the powerhouse team everyone loves to hate, and an <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/08/13/mount-carmel-jordan-lynch-ihsa" >IHSA practice-rule violation</a> in early August set the drama in motion early.</p><p>“The winning we’ve done comes with the hate,” Igwebuike said. “They are going to hate you, and then they will love you. We need to keep grinding and get this fifth state title. Pressure is a privilege. We’ve been speaking about that all offseason.”</p><p>Every successful program keeps the intensity high in practice and on game day. But the overall mood around Mount Carmel in the preseason feels the same as the past several years. Lynch keeps things casual, joking with the players lounging on the couch in his office before practice.</p><p>“People say if it isn’t broken, there is no reason to fix it,” Lynch said. “We believe if it is not broken, break it. There are always new things people are doing to try and beat you. People are studying Mount Carmel, and they are studying us year-round. We have to break it. We have to find a new way of doing things. That has been our approach.”</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-510000" name="module-510000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b>Mount Carmel’s college talent</b><br><br><b>Committed players</b><br><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-95749d70-9b2c-11f1-bfea-f973856c3b72"><li>WR Quentin Burrell, Sr. (Michigan)</li><li>LB Sergio Caleros, Sr. (Chicago State)</li><li>OT Chase Clark, Sr. (Purdue)</li><li>DE Darin Graham, Sr. (Wisconsin)</li><li>DB Tavares Harrington, Sr. (Michigan)</li><li>LB Roman Igwebuike, Sr. (Notre Dame)</li><li>DB Isaac Saldana, Sr. (South Dakota State)</li><li>RB Nathan Samuels, Sr. (Lindenwood)</li></ul><b>Players with Power Four offers</b><br><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-95749d71-9b2c-11f1-bfea-f973856c3b72"><li>QB Thomas Elliott, So.</li><li>DL Emmanuel McMoore, Jr.</li><li>OL Piotr Nakonieczny, So.</li><li>DE London Owens, Jr.</li><li>WR Marshaun Thornton, Jr. </li><li>OL Jesus Tinajero, So.</li><li>OL Caleb Tucker, Jr.</li><li>OL Kirk Turner, Jr.</li></ul><b>Players with college offers</b><br><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-95749d72-9b2c-11f1-bfea-f973856c3b72"><li>LB Corey McCullough, Jr.</li><li>S Brandon Rogers, Sr.</li><li>WR Duran Sims, Sr.</li></ul></div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Cubs’ late-inning bullpen puzzle: Daniel Palencia back soon, Jacob Webb dominates, Ryan Zeferjahn gets hit
entries.summary: <p><b>Craig Counsell</b> has already made it clear he plans to keep using <b>Jacob Webb</b> as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ go-to reliever.</p><p>“There’s nobody I’d rather have out there,” the skipper said after the righty stretched his streak of scoreless appearances to 22 games Monday.</p><p>But there is a late-inning bullpen puzzle to put together as the season’s most important games get closer and playoff baseball casts a glaring spotlight on high-leverage moments.</p><p><b>Daniel Palencia</b> is due back in the coming days. Counsell didn’t get any more specific than saying that Palencia will be activated from the injured list “soon,” but the righty fireballer’s minor league rehab assignment is done at the end of a two-month stay on the IL with elbow inflammation.</p><p>The manager previously said <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-daniel-palencia-jacob-webb-closer-craig-counsell-injury-rehab-kevin-gausman-trade-blue-jays-nl-central-standings-brewers" >the Cubs will be “flexible” deploying Palencia</a>, who has only logged 16⅔ innings this season, and trying to grow that number is Priority No. 1.</p><p>Plus, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/12/cubs-jacob-webb-closer-bullpen-relief-pitcher-craig-counsell-daniel-palencia-ryan-rolison-trent-thornton" >Webb’s been that good</a>, coming into Tuesday with a 2.29 ERA that ranked in the top 20 in baseball among pitchers with at least 50 innings pitched this year.</p><p>Elsewhere in the ‘pen, righty <b>Ryan Zeferjahn</b> had another tough night Monday, surrendering a go-ahead homer in the eighth inning of the Cubs’ win over the White Sox.</p><p><b>Jed Hoyer</b>’s front office <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-ryan-zeferjahn-bullpen-moises-ballesteros-trade-deadline-angels" >made Zeferjahn its late-inning bullpen addition</a> at the trade deadline, sending young slugger <b>Moises Ballesteros</b> to the Angels to net a reliable high-leverage arm. But Zeferjahn has given up five runs in six appearances since the trade, with an 8.44 ERA in 5⅓ innings as a Cub.</p><p>“We’ve seen what we thought we’d see,” Counsell said Tuesday. “It’s a little confusing on some of the pitches that have gotten hit so far. We’ll keep trying to dig into that. I like what he’s offering.</p><p>“The pitch [Monday] night wasn’t a bad pitch.”</p><p>Then there’s lefty <b>David Peterson</b>, suddenly part of the team’s relief corps after being bumped from the rotation by righty <b>Edward Cabrera</b> on Sunday. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/cubs-injuries-dansby-swanson-oblique-edward-cabrera-blister-nico-hoerner-pedro-ramizrez-craig-counsell-david-peterson-javier-assad-rotation-bullpen" >Cabrera has since returned to the injured list</a>, but Peterson was used in relief Monday, facing four batters and getting four outs.</p><p>Whether Peterson, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/28/cubs-david-peterson-mlb-trade-deadline-mets-jed-hoyer-pitching-staff-rotation-craig-counsell-ground-ball-rate" >who has been effective as a starter</a>, makes a quick return to the rotation remains to be seen.</p><p>“David has handled this situation really well,” Counsell said. “You understand that we’re trying to do something that’s really hard to do, and it’s going to require some kind of special effort from each one of us.”</p><h3><b>Pick your poison</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Should White Sox manager <b>Will Venable</b> have intentionally walked <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b> on Monday night?</p><p>It’s an easy decision to second guess after the Cubs’ center fielder <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/pete-crow-armstrongs-walk-off-homer-gives-cubs-win-over-white-sox-in-back-and-forth-crosstown-clash" >hit a walk-off homer</a>. But it’s easy to empathize with Venable, because the alternative wasn’t too appealing: facing right fielder <b>Seiya Suzuki</b>, who also homered earlier in the game.</p><p>Crow-Armstrong is an MVP candidate, so it might be easy to miss <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/23/seiya-suzuki-walk-up-music-frank-sinatra-my-way-free-agent-contract-home-runs-lineup-payroll" >what Suzuki has done</a>. He’s been among the sport’s most productive players, too, coming into Tuesday with a 135 wRC-plus that ranked 17th among qualified hitters.</p><p>“That’s why they’re hitting next to each other because you try to make managers’ decisions really hard. That’s kind of the point,” Counsell said. “I really believe Seiya, quietly, has been super consistent this year and has had a really good season. Pete’s just been that much better.</p><p>“It’s hard to say, but he’s been so good that it feels like there’s a gap. But Seiya’s been awesome this year. He’s having a great season.”</p><h3><b>Shaw facts</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Utility man <b>Matt Shaw</b>, who’s been <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/11/cubs-matt-shaw-injury-hand-sprain-injured-list-rehab-shota-imanaga-home-runs-nationals-edward-cabrera-daniel-palencia" >out since late June with a hand sprain</a>, will begin a minor league rehab assignment with Triple-A Iowa on Wednesday.</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" entries.title: Dansby Swanson’s presence will be part of Cubs’ efforts to weather his absence: ‘He turns into another coach’
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> will spend the next four weeks without their starting shortstop, no small thing in the middle of a playoff race.</p><p>Dansby Swanson is a critical part of the Cubs’ championship puzzle, playing Gold Glove defense at one of the sport’s premier positions and, if at times quietly, providing ample offensive production. He came into Tuesday fourth on the roster with 18 home runs.</p><p>So keeping the team’s best-in-baseball defense humming and one of the top-scoring offenses in the game firing on as many cylinders as possible — all while trying to close the gap with the division-leading Brewers — becomes tougher with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/cubs-injuries-dansby-swanson-oblique-edward-cabrera-blister-nico-hoerner-pedro-ramizrez-craig-counsell-david-peterson-javier-assad-rotation-bullpen" >Swanson sidelined by an oblique strain</a>.</p><p>“It’s a huge deal,” said second baseman Nico Hoerner, who has taken over everyday shortstop duties in Swanson’s absence. “He’s at the heart of everything we do. It shows up in his production on both sides of the ball, but also all the things that you can’t measure: the consistency and the person.</p><p>“Obviously, he’s going to stay involved as much as he can. He loves the game. He loves this group. But we’re going to really miss him a lot.”</p><p>Yes, it seems Swanson, even while kept from the field, has no plans to stop being an impact for a Cubs team chasing a championship.</p><p>Even before he got hurt, there were descriptions of the important conversations teammates were having with Swanson. Now, that will be among his chief contributions while he recovers.</p><p>“He’s a guy that I really respect the knowledge of the game that he has,” third baseman Alex Bregman said last week. “We bounce things off of each other over the course of the season, whether it’s about us or our teammates, hitting, defense, pitching, whatever it may be.</p><p>“We’re looking to do one thing, and that’s win. Both of us, our whole career, have won. That’s what wakes us up in the morning every single day is to win baseball games.”</p><p>It’s enough that Swanson is already being looked at as not just a teammate but something of an addition to the Cubs’ coaching staff.</p><p>“He was hurt a couple years ago … he was out for a little bit,” left fielder Ian Happ said Monday. “He turns into another coach. So he’ll be around, he’ll be giving his input.”</p><p>On the field, the Cubs will lean on Hoerner, a Gold Glove infielder in his own right who’s played shortstop in the big leagues before, if not too much of it in recent seasons. Pedro Ramirez, a rookie who has impressed with the bat and the glove as a part-timer this season, will shoulder a bigger load as the everyday second baseman for the next few weeks.</p><p>“It is different playing short,” Hoerner said. “It’s a harder position. There’s a little more, physically, behind it. … I’m comfortable there. I’m confident in being able to play the position.</p><p>“Pedro from early in spring training has shown so much maturity and confidence, a good sense of humor. He’s a guy that seems to do everything on a baseball field at a high level. We’re very confident in him.”</p><p>It’s a new wrinkle for the Cubs, who despite nearly being buried by an avalanche of pitching injuries have been at nearly full strength on the position-player side of things for the vast majority of the campaign.</p><p>They managed to weather that barrage of pitching injuries, though, and are currently one of the game’s best teams, waking up Tuesday with the fifth best record in the sport after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/pete-crow-armstrongs-walk-off-homer-gives-cubs-win-over-white-sox-in-back-and-forth-crosstown-clash" >Monday’s thrilling walk-off, extra-inning win</a> over the Crosstown-rival White Sox.</p><p>Now, they’ll have to weather Swanson’s absence as they get closer and closer to crunch time: the home stretch of the regular season and the playoffs.</p><p>But at least Swanson will still be doing what he can to help the Cubs reach baseball’s mountaintop.</p><p>“That’s just who he is,” Hoerner said. “He’s invested in this team and the people on this team. I’m sure it’s incredibly frustrating for him to not be able to be out there. But we all know where his priorities lie, and it’s fun that how he wants to spend his time and energy is with the group.”</p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 entries.title: Nectarine and blackberry cobbler delivers a balance of fresh summer flavor and comforting, homemade goodness
entries.summary: <p>A great cobbler is all about the contrast between bubbling, juicy fruit and a golden, baked biscuit topping. In this recipe, ripe nectarines and plump blackberries create a sweet-tart filling that bubbles beneath a layer of tender, buttery drop biscuits with toasty edges. Rather than rolling or cutting the dough, spoonfuls of soft biscuit dough are dropped directly over the fruit, forming crisp, golden mounds with fluffy centers.</p><p>As the cobbler bakes, the biscuits soak up just enough of the bubbling nectarine and blackberry juices while still holding their buttery texture. The result is a perfect contrast of jammy fruit and light, flaky biscuits, delivering a balance of fresh summer flavor and comforting, homemade goodness.</p><p>Serve it warm on its own or with a scoop of vanilla ice cream for a timeless seasonal dessert.</p><h3>Nectarine and Blackberry Cobbler</h3><p><b>Active time:</b> 30 to 40 minutes<br><b>Total time:</b> 1 hour and 15 minutes<br><b>Yield:</b> 6 to 8 servings</p><p><b>Ingredients</b></p><p>8 ripe nectarines, pitted, sliced about 1/4-inch thick<br>8 ounces fresh blackberries<br>1/3 cup sugar<br>1 tablespoon all-purpose flour<br>1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice<br>1 teaspoon finely grated lemon zest<br>1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom<br>Pinch of kosher salt<br>1 tablespoon cold unsalted butter cut into small pieces (to dot)</p><p><b>Topping</b></p><p>1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour<br>1/2 cup sugar, plus 2 tablespoons for sprinkling<br>2 teaspoons baking powder<br>1/2 teaspoon baking soda<br>1/2 teaspoon kosher salt<br>1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom<br>6 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cubed<br>3/4 cup buttermilk<br>1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract</p><p><b>Directions</b></p><p>Heat the oven to 350 degrees.</p><p>Combine the nectarines, blackberries, sugar, flour, lemon juice, zest, cardamom and salt in a large bowl. Toss gently to coat.</p><p>Spread the fruit in an 8-by-10-inch baking dish. Dot the top of the fruit with the pieces of butter.</p><p>Make the topping: Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cardamom in a bowl. Whisk to blend.</p><p>Add the butter: With your fingertips, rub the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse meal with only pea-sized chunks of butter remaining.</p><p>Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and add the buttermilk and vanilla. Mix with a spatula until the dry ingredients are just moistened; do not overmix.</p><p>Scoop the biscuit batter over the fruit in 10 to 12 dollops. Sprinkle the remaining 2 tablespoons sugar over the tops of the biscuits.</p><p>Bake until the biscuits are golden brown and the fruit filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 minutes. Cool for at least an hour. Serve with vanilla ice cream.</p><p><i>Lynda Balslev is an award-winning writer, cookbook author and recipe developer, and authors the blog TasteFood.</i></p>

entries.title: $250,000 reward offered for information in 2018 disappearance of pregnant postal worker
entries.summary: <p>The United States Postal Inspection Service is increasing a reward for information that would “aid in the investigation” of the 2018 disappearance of a pregnant postal worker to $250,000.</p><p>It’s a tenfold increase from the reward offered by the federal law enforcement agency a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2019/7/15/20695331/missing-woman-kierra-coles-family-seeks-public-help" target="_blank" ><u>year after her disappearance</u></a>.</p><p>Kierra Coles, then 26 years old and three months pregnant, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2018/10/19/18421615/police-foul-play-suspected-in-case-of-missing-pregnant-woman-kierra-coles" target="_blank" ><u>went missing Oct. 2, 2018</u></a><u>,</u> after leaving her South Chicago apartment near 82nd Street and Coles Avenue, according to a missing person alert from the agency. She would now be 34 years old.</p><p>In the alert, the U.S. postal service worker is described as a 125-pound, 5-foot-4 Black woman with brown eyes and black hair, police said. She has a tattoo of a heart on her right hand and another that reads “Lucky Libra” on her back.</p><p>In the years since her disappearance, Coles' loved ones have repeatedly called for the case to be <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2021/9/24/22692446/kierra-coles-gabby-petito-jelani-day-postal-service-missing-persons-illinois-state-university" target="_blank" ><u>treated with the same urgency</u></a> as the disappearance of Gabby Petito, a white YouTuber whose disappearance in 2021 made national headlines and triggered a nationwide search, ultimately leading to her remains being found.</p><p>They’ve also made calls for information alongside the families of other missing people through celebrations of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2021/9/24/22692446/kierra-coles-gabby-petito-jelani-day-postal-service-missing-persons-illinois-state-university" target="_blank" ><u>her birthday</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2024/05/12/mothers-day-moms-missing-children-crime-police-cpd-chicago-loop-investigation-city-hall" target="_blank" ><u>Mother’s Day</u></a>.</p><p>Anyone with information is asked to call investigators at 877-876-2455 referencing case number 2693502.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div
